أبانة (אֲבָנָה؛ Abana) أحد نهري دمشق في: Abana (אֲבָנָה; Abana) is one of the two rivers of Damascus in 2 Kings 5. Some proposals connect it with a meaning of stone or rock, with differing readings.
أرنون (אַרְנוֹן؛ Arnon) اسم مجرى مائي كب: Arnon (אַרְנוֹן; Arnon) is the name of a large watercourse east of the Dead Sea, and linguistic proposals connect it with a torrent or rushing flow.
أمر فرعون بطرح الأولاد، ووُضع موسى في سف: Pharaoh ordered that the male children be cast into it, Moses was placed in a basket upon the water, and then the waters of the Nile turned to blood in the first plague. References: Exodus 1:22; 2:3-10; 7:14-25; Isaiah 19; Ezekiel 29.

اختيار لوط، عبور يشوع، عبور إيليا وأليشع: Lot's choice, Joshua's crossing, the crossing of Elijah and Elisha, Naaman's healing, John's baptism, and the baptism of Jesus. References: Genesis 13:10; Joshua 3; 2 Kings 2:8-14; 5:10-14; Matthew 3:13-17.

الخابور (חָבוֹר؛ Habor/Khabur) رافد للفر: Habor (חָבוֹר; Habor/Khabur) is a tributary of the Euphrates in northern Mesopotamia, and a well-known geographical name in the ancient region.
الفرات (פְּרָת؛ Pĕrāth؛ الأكادية Purattu: The Euphrates (פְּרָת; Pĕrāth; Akkadian Purattu) is one of the great rivers of the ancient Near East.
النيل هو شريان مصر الزراعي والحضاري، وتد: The Nile is the agricultural and civilizational artery of Egypt, and the story of Moses in Exodus 1-7 revolves around it, and the prophecies also use it when speaking of Egypt.
بصور (בְּשׂוֹר؛ Besor) اسم وادٍ أو مجرى: Besor (בְּשׂוֹר; Besor) is the name of a wadi or watercourse in southern Judah. Linking it to the root of "good news" is a linguistic suggestion that alone does not suffice to explain the story.
بقي 200 رجل عند النهر من شدة التعب، وتاب: 200 men stayed by the brook out of exhaustion, while 400 continued on, and then David decided that the share of those who stayed should be equal to the share of those who fought. Reference: 1 Samuel 30:9-24.

تسمح صورة النهر المتدفق بقراءة لاهوتية ع: The image of the flowing river allows for a theological reading concerning the life that God grants, but it does not become evidence for identifying the river in modern terms.
تظهر الطبيعة هنا داخل فعل الدينونة والنص: Nature appears here within the act of judgment and victory, but the text's judgments upon ancient peoples must not be transferred to contemporary religious violence.
تكشف حدوده أن الوعد في الكتاب مرتبط بتعي: Its boundaries reveal that the promise in the Scripture is bound up with the designation of responsibilities and boundaries, not with mere open possession without limits.
تكوين 2؛ والسياق الكتابي المذكور في الدر: Genesis 2; and the biblical context mentioned in the study.
توضح القصة الفرق بين توقعات الإنسان وطري: The story clarifies the difference between human expectations and God's way of working, without turning it into a judgment on the worth of rivers or peoples.
تُظهر عودة دجلة في دانيال امتداد الجغراف: The reappearance of the Tigris in Daniel shows the extension of biblical geography from creation to the time of the exile and prophetic revelation, without assuming that the place alone interprets the vision.
جرف قيشون جيش سيسرا في رواية دبورة وبارا: The Kishon swept away Sisera's army in the account of Deborah and Barak, and then the prophets of Baal were taken to it after Elijah's confrontation. The text does not establish that water alone was the cause of victory.
جيحون (גִּיחוֹן؛ Gihon) اسم يرتبط لغويًا: Gihon (גִּיחוֹן; Gihon) is a name linguistically connected with the idea of gushing forth or bursting out, while the interpretive etymology remains inconclusive.
حزقيال هو الشخصية المحورية، ومعه المسبيو: Ezekiel is the central figure, along with the Jewish exiles. The text does not describe the river as a place of worship, but as part of the reality of exile in which the revelation came.
حِدِّقِل (חִדֶּקֶל؛ Hiddekel) هو الاسم ا: Hiddekel (חִדֶּקֶל; Hiddekel) is the Hebrew name for the Tigris. It is traditionally linked with swiftness or rushing, with caution against making the etymology the sole basis for interpretation.

زارد (זֶרֶד؛ Zered) يُقترح أن يرتبط بمجر: Zered (זֶרֶד; Zered) is suggested to be associated with a willow stream or torrent, without full etymological certainty.

عبر يعقوب النهر ليلًا، وبقي وحده وصارع ح: Jacob crossed the river at night, remained alone, wrestled until dawn, and received the name Israel. Reference: Genesis 32:22-32. It also appears in Numbers 21:24 and Deuteronomy 2:37.
عبره إسرائيل في طريقه إلى شرق الأردن في: Israel crossed it on the way to the east side of the Jordan in the time of Moses, and the song of victory in Numbers 21 is associated with it. The persons are Moses, Israel, and Sihon within the context of the text.
عبره بنو إسرائيل بعد مرحلة التيه، في سيا: The children of Israel crossed it after the stage of wandering, in the context of the transition of the generation. References: Numbers 21:12-13; Deuteronomy 2:13-14.
عبور يبوق حدث جغرافي وصراع شخصي في آن وا: The crossing of the Jabbok is both a geographical event and a personal struggle at once, but what the text establishes is Jacob's transformation into Israel, not a general rule about every spiritual crossing.

فيشون (פִּישׁוֹן؛ Pishon). يُقترح ربطه ب: Pishon (פִּישׁוֹן; Pishon). It has been proposed that it be linked to the idea of spreading or flowing, but the etymology is not certain; therefore, no definitive conclusion is built upon it.
قارن نعمان أبانة وفرفر بمياه إسرائيل قبل: Naaman compared Abana and Pharpar with the waters of Israel before he obeyed and washed in the Jordan. Reference: 2 Kings 5:1-14. Persons: Naaman, Elisha, Gehazi, and Naaman's servant girl.
قوة المدخل في أن حضور الله لا يُحصر جغرا: The strength of this entry lies in the fact that God's presence is not geographically confined to Jerusalem; this is a theological conclusion based on the scene of the vision, not a nullification of the importance of the temple in the book of Ezekiel.
قيشون (קִישׁוֹן؛ Qishon) نهر سهل يزرعيل: Kishon (קִישׁוֹן; Qishon) is the river of the plain of Jezreel flowing toward the Bay of Acre. Its proposed etymology is connected with the idea of winding or meandering.
كان حزقيال بين المسبيين عند نهر كبار، وه: Ezekiel was among the exiles by the river Chebar, and there he saw visions of the glory of the Lord. References: Ezekiel 1:1-3; 3:23; 10:15; 43:3.
كبار (נְהַר־כְּבָר؛ Chebar) مجرى أو قناة: Chebar (נְהַר־כְּבָר; Chebar) is a watercourse or canal in the land of Babylon. Cuneiform research suggests its connection with the canal nāru kabari, but its precise location remains a matter of debate.

يرده 2 ملوك 17:6 ضمن وجهات السبي الآشوري: 2 Kings 17:6 mentions it among the destinations of the Assyrian exile: Halah, and Habor the river of Gozan, and the cities of the Medes.
